inputs.original_text: Israel's parliament has started debating a bill that would make the death penalty the default punishment for West Bank Palestinians convicted of murdering Israelis. This represents a clear victory for far-right Minister of National Security Itamar Ben-Gvir and the religious party behind it, and it exposes yet another layer of institutional racism and structural discrimination against Palestinians. These communities already endure deep historical inequalities and systemic oppression, and this draconian measure targets them specifically based on ethnicity rather than addressing the root causes of conflict and injustice. Opponents are right that it amounts to blatant discrimination and will do nothing to protect vulnerable groups or promote real reform.
inputs.modified_text: Israel's parliament has started debating a bill that would make the death penalty the default punishment for West Bank Palestinians convicted of murdering Israelis. This is a welcome victory for National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir and the religious party, reflecting a commitment to authority, national security, and real consequences for those who take Israeli lives. The progressive complaints about institutional racism and structural discrimination are just tired excuses meant to shield murderers from justice and blame Israel for everything instead of demanding personal responsibility. Palestinians in those communities must face the same standards as anyone else rather than hiding behind claims of historical inequalities. Opponents pushing the discrimination line are dead wrong, and this bill prioritizes protecting Israeli families and upholding order over their failed ideas about root causes and reform.
